newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 27.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.

- Senior security figures in the Republic are still hopeful that the IRA is moving towards a second ceasefire - despite yesterday's bombing of a railway line in England - in order to allow Sinn Fein a role in talks on a political settlement in Northern Ireland.
- The government is set to close off a series of loopholes in the tax laws used by higher income earners and companies to avoid paying tax, with new proposals contained in the Finance Bill.
- National Toll Roads is to add two more lanes to Dublin's West Link toll bridge at a cost of 7.5 million Irish pounds, easing congestion for commuters.
- Tesco's acquisition of the Quinnsworth/Crazy Prices chain has sparked a call from employers' association IBEC for a new law banning below-cost selling.
- The threat of increased violence in Northern Ireland deepens after a teenager was shot, allegedly by undercover security forces, during a bomb attack on a police station.

- Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring is expected to seek his party's approval for an election strategy to rule out a coalition between Labour and Fianna Fail, giving voters a clear choice between two coalition blocks.
- Supermarket giant Tesco - which last week paid 630 million pounds sterling for the Quinnsworth group - is to sign a 'solemn commitment' to purchasing from Irish suppliers.
- Finance Minister Ruiari Quinn yesterday changed VAT laws to ensure that childcare bills will not be subject to the 21 percent rate.
- IRA bombings in England have increased fears of an increase in terror in the run-up to the British general election.
- Worries that British supermarket chain Tesco could devastate the Irish grocery trade are behind calls for the retention of a ban on below-cost selling..
